mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strengthening demand, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances with sustained 3-month increase in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds the 10-year Treasury yield, it signals an inverted yield curve, which is a predictor of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances with an inverted yield curve.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals strong consumer demand and labor market health, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances with the described interaction.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals increased economic activity, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances with INDPRO MoM > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances with sustained 3-month increase in PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening economy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 40% of instances with GDPC1 QoQ < -0.5%.
